name: Japan Masters
stakes: This week is crucial for India to consolidate ranking points, build momentum, and test their mettle against top international competition ahead of the season's final stretch.
summary:
India's contingent at the Japan Masters Super 500 event sees a mix of established stars and promising talent looking to make a deep run. Men's Doubles pair Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty, seeded fourth, lead the charge as India's top-ranked pair, hoping to build on their consistent performances this season. Their R32 opponent is yet to be determined.

In the Men's Singles, Lakshya Sen arrives with significant momentum, having just clinched the Hylo Open title—he's already secured his spot in the Round of 16 here after defeating Yu Jen. Veteran Kidambi Srikanth also showed his mettle, navigating a tough opening match against Rasmus Gemke to advance to the pre-quarterfinals. PV Sindhu, a consistent presence at the top, will be looking to kickstart her campaign, while Treesa Jolly and Gayatri Gopichand continue their journey as a rising force in Women's Doubles. HS Prannoy and Malvika Bansod round out the Indian challenge, seeking crucial ranking points and valuable experience against a strong international field.
